question.problem:
The heights of oak trees in a park are normally distributed with a mean of $\mu $ feet and a standard deviation of $8$ feet. Additionally, $25%$ of the trees are shorter than $45$ feet. Find the percentage of trees taller than $50$ feet. **Round your answer to two decimal places.**

*Hint: A table of values of ${Φ}^{-1}(p)$ for different values of $p$ is given below, where $p=Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution.*

| $p$ | $\,0.01\,$ | $\,0.03\,$ | $\,0.05\,$ | $\,0.10\,$ | $\,0.20\,$ | $\,0.25\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${Φ}^{-1}(p)$ | $\,-2.3263\,$ | $\,-1.8808\,$ | $\,-1.6449\,$ | $\,-1.2816\,$ | $\,-0.8416\,$ | $\,-0.6745\,$ |

*In addition, you're given the following table of values for $p=Φ(z).$*

| $z$ | $\,0.03\,$ | $\,0.04\,$ | $\,0.05\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,-0.2\,$ | $\,0.4090\,$ | $\,0.4052\,$ | $\,0.4013\,$ |
| $\,-0.1\,$ | $\,0.4483\,$ | $\,0.4443\,$ | $\,0.4404\,$ |
| $\,-0.0\,$ | $\,0.4880\,$ | $\,0.4840\,$ | $\,0.4801\,$ |

Approximately
{{field-1}}$%$ of the trees are taller than $50$ feet.
